meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_2F_2506, sat 5 June 2025). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: q1(c) tagged decimals following the house rule in docs/coding-a-paper.md ('place value ... tagged decimals'). The question's distractors are explicitly decimal place-value terms (tenths, hundredths, thousandths) even though the answer is an integer place.

q1(a),(b),(e) and q4 tagged simple_arithmetic / decimals: ordering large integers, writing a number in words, and reading or marking a number line. Reading a scale was reviewed for the taxonomy and DECIDED NOT TO ADD (docs/coding-a-paper.md), so these stay on the arithmetic nodes.
q13 tagged exact_calculations: that skill's own example is 'use your calculator ... and write down all the figures in your calculator display', which is this question exactly.

q2(a) and q11(a) tagged gathering_and_organising_data: a tally/frequency table and a two-way table. 4MA1 Foundation 6.1 limits data presentation to 'pictograms, bar charts and pie charts, and only two-way tables', so two-way tables carry more of this paper than they would on a GCSE one.
q7 tagged proportion rather than simultaneous_equations: the mark scheme's route is unitary (cost of one cupcake, then subtract), not elimination.
q10(b) tagged systematic_listing: enumerating the positive odd values satisfying a bound. inequalities would claim the solving of an inequality, which is not what the marks are for.
q19(b) is a ROTATION per the mark scheme, not an enlargement — the B2 partial for 'enlargement' is a wrong-answer allowance, not the answer.
No arithmetic series on this paper. GAP-CANDIDATE tally unchanged.
